items.title: Cache hints don't reach other APIs
items.body_md: Only Messages takes `cache_control`. When a Messages request reaches a model on another API, the AI Gateway drops each cache hint and lists `cache_control` in the removed parameters. The answer is the same, but the provider doesn't cache your prompt, so a long repeated prompt costs more.

items.title: Converse cache points keep a request on Converse
items.body_md: A Converse request with a `cachePoint` block only reaches Converse models. Remove the cache point to let the request reach models on other APIs.

items.title: Messages requests always get max_tokens
items.body_md: Messages requires `max_tokens`. When your request sets no output limit, the AI Gateway sends the model's maximum output tokens. Set an output limit yourself if you want a long answer to stop at a known length.

items.title: Responses requests are sent with store off
items.body_md: A request from another API reaches a Responses model with `store: false`. Your client can't read a stored response back, so the provider doesn't keep one.

items.title: Messages caps temperature at 1
items.body_md: Messages takes a temperature from 0 to 1. A higher temperature from another API reaches a Messages model as 1, and the AI Gateway reports it as clamped.

items.title: Messages drops temperature while thinking is on
items.body_md: Claude models refuse `temperature` while extended thinking is on. When your request sets a thinking budget and reaches a Messages model, the AI Gateway drops the temperature and reports it as removed by the model.

items.title: A thinking budget shrinks to fit the output limit
items.body_md: Messages counts thinking inside `max_tokens`. When your thinking budget is larger than the output limit, the AI Gateway lowers the budget so the model still has room to answer, and reports the change.

items.title: Effort becomes a thinking budget on older Claude models
items.body_md: Claude Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5, and Opus 4.1 take a thinking budget, not an effort. When `reasoning_effort`, `reasoning.effort`, or `thinkingLevel` reaches one of these models, the AI Gateway turns on thinking with a budget for that level: 1,024 tokens for minimal and low, 4,096 for medium, 16,384 for high, and 32,000 for xhigh and max. A budget only approximates an effort, so the AI Gateway reports the effort as clamped. Newer Claude models take the effort itself, at the nearest level the model accepts.

items.title: Max effort becomes high
items.body_md: Only Messages has a `max` effort. Chat Completions, Responses, and generateContent get `high` instead, and the AI Gateway reports the effort as clamped.

items.title: Responses needs an output limit of at least 16
items.body_md: Responses rejects an output limit below 16 tokens. A smaller limit from another API reaches a Responses model as 16.

items.title: Reasoning from another provider is dropped
items.body_md: Providers sign their reasoning and reject a signature from anyone else. When your conversation replays reasoning that one API produced and the request reaches a model on another API, the AI Gateway drops that reasoning and reports `reasoning` as removed. The rest of the turn still reaches the model.

items.title: Some tool schema settings are dropped
items.body_md: Each API reads tool schemas a little differently. The AI Gateway drops `propertyOrdering` from a Gemini schema, because it only orders Gemini's own output. It drops `strict` for APIs that have no strict mode, so the model can return arguments that don't match your schema exactly. Both show up in the removed parameters.

items.title: Image detail only reaches OpenAI APIs
items.body_md: Only Chat Completions and Responses take an image `detail` setting. Other APIs get the image at their default detail, and the AI Gateway reports `detail` as removed.

items.title: Legacy functions stay on Chat Completions
items.body_md: A Chat Completions request with `functions` or `function_call` only reaches Chat Completions models. Switch to `tools` and `tool_choice` to reach models on other APIs.

items.title: previous_response_id only reaches Responses
items.body_md: `previous_response_id`, `conversation`, `prompt`, and `background` point to state that a Responses provider stores for your account. No other API can read it, so these requests only reach Responses models. Send the full conversation instead to reach models on other APIs.

items.title: Converse guardrails and stored prompts stay on Converse
items.body_md: `guardrailConfig`, `outputConfig.textFormat`, and `promptVariables` have no match on other APIs. Without them, an answer would skip your guardrail or come back in the wrong shape, so these requests only reach Converse models.

items.title: Requests for more than one answer stay on their own API
items.body_md: Only Chat Completions and generateContent return several answers to one request. A request with `n` or `candidateCount` above 1 only reaches models on its own API.

items.title: JSON output doesn't reach Converse models yet
items.body_md: Converse takes a JSON schema in `outputConfig.textFormat`, but the AI Gateway doesn't translate a schema to or from it yet. A request that asks for JSON output doesn't reach Converse models. Messages takes a JSON schema but not plain JSON mode, so a request for JSON without a schema doesn't reach Messages models either.

items.title: Web search needs an API that searches
items.body_md: Converse runs no web search, and Chat Completions only searches through providers that offer it. A request that asks for a web search doesn't reach those models, because an answer without the search isn't the answer you asked for.

items.title: Code tools only reach APIs that run Python
items.body_md: The AI Gateway translates a hosted code tool only between APIs whose tool runs Python: Responses and generateContent reach each other, and a Messages request with `code_execution_20250522` reaches either. Chat Completions and Converse run no code, and Claude runs code through Bash, so a request with a code tool doesn't reach those models.

items.title: Other hosted tools stay on their own API
items.body_md: Hosted tools like file search, image generation, URL context, Bash, the text editor, and web fetch run inside one provider. A request with one of them only reaches models on its own API.

items.title: Remote MCP servers move only between Responses and Messages
items.body_md: A Responses `mcp` tool and a Messages MCP server (`mcp_servers` with its `mcp_toolset`) translate into each other, and reach no other API. The Responses tool must set `require_approval` to `never`, because Messages has no approval step. A Responses request only reaches Claude models on Anthropic's own API, and a Messages request only reaches OpenAI's own API, because other providers don't call remote MCP servers.

items.title: Use responseJsonSchema to reach other APIs
items.body_md: `generationConfig.responseSchema` takes Gemini's OpenAPI schema, which other APIs can't read. A request with it only reaches Gemini models. Send the same schema as JSON Schema in `responseJsonSchema` to reach models on other APIs.
